articles.title: Dollar General overcharged shoppers, FTC and states allege in lawsuit
articles.summary: Oct 26 (Reuters) - Dollar General repeatedly charged more than advertised prices even after ‌receiving tens of thousands of consumer complaints, ‌the US Fede...
articles.body:
Oct 26 (Reuters) - Dollar General repeatedly charged more than advertised prices even after ‌receiving tens of thousands of consumer complaints, ‌the US Federal Trade Commission and 20 states alleged in a ​lawsuit filed on Monday.

Dollar General, which appeals to low-income consumers with bargain prices, made millions of dollars by failing to honor prices advertised on fliers and ‌shelves at checkout, ⁠the FTC and states allege.

The discount retailer's stock was down more than 4% on ⁠Monday afternoon.

"Dollar General has, for years, repeatedly mislabeled prices, overcharged consumers and failed to correct the issue ​despite extensive ​corporate knowledge of the ​problem," the FTC and ‌states said in a statement.

Representatives for Dollar General did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

The lawsuit cited numerous complaints from consumers, failed inspections conducted by state authorities, and undercover shopping sprees conducted ‌by the FTC.

Portions of the ​lawsuit detailing the company's knowledge ​of the practices ​were largely redacted.

California joined the FTC ‌lawsuit along with Florida, Illinois, ​Michigan, Ohio, North ​Carolina, Tennessee and 13 other states.

Since 2019, Dollar General has paid $6 million in settlements with ​six states over ‌inaccurate pricing, according to the complaint.

(Reporting by ​Katharine Jackson and Susan Heavey; Editing by Doina ​Chiacu and Bill Berkrot)

images.caption: A view of a Dollar General store in Mount Rainier, Maryland, U.S., June 1, 2021. REUTERS/Erin Scott · Reuters

articles.title: Taxação de bilionários: eleitores da Califórnia podem aprovar primeiro imposto do tipo no mundo? | G1
articles.standfirst: Os eleitores estão prestes a decidir se os super-ricos entre eles devem entregar bilhões de dólares para financiar melhorias no sistema de saúde.
articles.summary: Os eleitores estão prestes a decidir se os super-ricos entre eles devem entregar bilhões de dólares para financiar melhorias no sistema de saúde.
articles.body:
Eleitores da Califórnia podem aprovar primeiro imposto do tipo no mundo? — Foto: Reuters via BBC

Poucos lugares no planeta têm tantos moradores ultrarricos quanto a Califórnia, estado americano conhecido pelo glamour, pelas mansões à beira-mar e por abrigar pessoas ricas e famosas.

Agora, os eleitores estão prestes a decidir se os super-ricos do estado — entre eles a magnata da mídia Oprah Winfrey, o presidente da Meta, Mark Zuckerberg , Kim Kardashian , cofundadora da Skims e estrela de reality shows, e o cineasta George Lucas — devem desembolsar bilhões de dólares para financiar melhorias na área da saúde.

A Proposição 40 tem como objetivo instituir um imposto único de 5% sobre o patrimônio líquido de todos os bilionários da Califórnia.

Há pouco mais de 200 pessoas nessa categoria no estado, mas isso não impediu que a proposta dividisse lideranças e levasse alguns de seus moradores ultrarricos a deixar a região. Um empresário bilionário afirma ter gerado empregos na Califórnia, mas diz que a proposta o fez se sentir "um pouco como se eu não fosse bem-vindo".

A votação também está dando aos cidadãos comuns a oportunidade de se manifestar sobre uma questão que provoca turbulência na política há décadas.

"Eu acredito que este é o primeiro imposto sobre bilionários — ou seja, um imposto sobre o patrimônio direcionado a uma parcela extremamente restrita da distribuição de riqueza", afirma Francesco Trebbi, professor de políticas públicas da Universidade da Califórnia em Berkeley. Ele destaca o caráter histórico da medida e como ela poderia ajudar a reduzir a desigualdade patrimonial no estado.

A Califórnia tem a maior economia entre os estados americanos e a quarta maior economia do mundo, superior às da Índia e do Reino Unido. O estado também abriga uma das maiores concentrações de bilionários do planeta. Ao mesmo tempo, tem a maior proporção de pessoas em situação de rua do país e uma das maiores desigualdades patrimoniais.

Os defensores da proposta argumentam que ela ajudaria a garantir que os ultrarricos contribuam com sua parcela justa de impostos e compensaria déficits no orçamento estadual. A iniciativa pretende arrecadar US$ 100 bilhões (cerca de R$ 496 bilhões) para compensar cortes no financiamento federal do sistema de saúde do estado.

Suzanne Jimenez, chefe de gabinete do Sindicato Internacional dos Empregados em Serviços — Trabalhadores da Saúde Unidos do Oeste (SEIU-UHW), que ajudou a liderar a campanha pela iniciativa, afirma que a medida é uma "solução de curto prazo" para os grandes cortes de recursos federais que a Califórnia deverá enfrentar em consequência do abrangente pacote tributário e de gastos do presidente dos Estados Unidos, Donald Trump.

"Se não fizermos nada, veremos nosso sistema de saúde entrar em colapso enquanto buscamos uma solução de longo prazo para financiá-lo", disse ela à BBC.

Os defensores da proposta argumentam que ela ajudaria a garantir que os ultrarricos contribuam com sua parcela justa de impostos e compensaria déficits no orçamento estadual. — Foto: Getty Image via BBC

Embora a proposta tenha muitos apoiadores — incluindo alguns bilionários, como Jensen Huang, CEO da Nvidia —, ela enfrenta forte oposição de diferentes figuras, de bilionários ao governador liberal do estado.

Sergey Brin, cofundador do Google, doou mais de US$ 100 milhões a uma organização política que financia medidas eleitorais capazes de bloquear o imposto sobre o patrimônio, segundo o Los Angeles Times.

O governador da Califórnia, Gavin Newsom, que está chegando ao fim de seu mandato, é talvez a liderança política mais importante a se opor à proposta. Ele manifestou preocupação de que a medida leve os ricos a deixar o estado, provocando a perda de receitas essenciais provenientes do imposto de renda.

Uma pesquisa realizada em setembro pelo Instituto de Estudos Governamentais de Berkeley e pelo Los Angeles Times constatou que a proposta ainda não conquistou claramente a maioria dos eleitores: 45% dos eleitores com maior probabilidade de votar eram favoráveis ao imposto, 42% eram contrários e 13% estavam indecisos.

A medida, submetida à votação em todo o estado, precisará ser aprovada pela maioria dos eleitores.

A Califórnia não é o primeiro lugar a considerar a possibilidade de tributar os ricos. Também na costa oeste, os eleitores do estado americano de Washington estão avaliando se aprovam ou rejeitam um "imposto sobre milionários": uma alíquota de 9,9% sobre rendimentos anuais superiores a US$ 1 milhão.

Embora os impostos sobre o patrimônio tenham sido relativamente comuns na Europa, eles perderam popularidade rapidamente e hoje existem em apenas três países europeus — Espanha, Noruega e Suíça —, afirma o dr. Kristian Niemietz, chefe de economia política do Instituto de Assuntos Econômicos.

Niemietz considera que os impostos sobre o patrimônio "dão mais trabalho do que valem a pena", pois criam dificuldades administrativas, desestimulam investimentos, provocam a saída de capitais e, no fim das contas, arrecadam pouco.

No caso da Noruega, uma organização de notícias local constatou que o aumento do imposto sobre o patrimônio levou mais super-ricos a deixar o país em 2022 do que nos 13 anos anteriores somados. Um estudo sobre a Suíça concluiu que um aumento de 0,1 ponto percentual na alíquota do imposto sobre o patrimônio reduziu em 3,5% o patrimônio tributável.

Se aprovada, a medida da Califórnia será aplicada retroativamente a pessoas com patrimônio líquido de pelo menos US$ 1 bilhão que residiam no estado em 1º de janeiro de 2026. Pelo menos seis dos mais de 200 bilionários da Califórnia teriam deixado o estado antes dessa data para evitar o imposto.

Entre eles estão os cofundadores do Google Larry Page e Sergey Brin, o investidor de capital de risco Peter Thiel, o ex-CEO da Uber Travis Kalanick e Don Hankey, fundador do Hankey Group.

Hankey, bilionário de Los Angeles que viveu toda a vida na Califórnia, disse à revista Forbes que se mudou para o estado de Nevada por causa da proposta de imposto sobre o patrimônio.

"Acho que criamos muitos empregos na Califórnia. Temos alguns milhares de pessoas trabalhando para nós e um plano de participação nos lucros. E preciso deixar o estado", afirmou. Ele acrescentou que a medida o fez sentir que não era "bem-vindo" no estado.

Segundo relatos, o cofundador do Google Sergey Brin doou mais de US$ 100 milhões a uma organização política que financia medidas eleitorais capazes de bloquear o imposto sobre o patrimônio. — Foto: Getty Images via BBC

Mark Zuckerberg , presidente-executivo da Meta, disse ao conselho de administração da empresa no mês passado que estava considerando transferir sua residência principal para fora da Califórnia por causa do imposto proposto.

Para evitar que ele deixe o estado — onde fica a sede da empresa —, a Meta concordou com um novo acordo de remuneração em ações que concede a Zuckerberg, cuja fortuna é estimada em mais de US$ 200 bilhões, ainda mais participações na companhia. O objetivo é compensá-lo pelos bilhões de dólares que perderia caso a medida fosse aprovada em novembro. Estimativas indicam que ele poderia ter de pagar até US$ 12,5 bilhões.

Andy Fang, cofundador da DoorDash, cuja fortuna é estimada em US$ 1,6 bilhão, classificou a medida como "estúpida" e escreveu na rede social X que "propostas como essa tornam irresponsável da minha parte não planejar deixar o estado".

Enquanto isso, o empresário Tom Steyer, que disputou sem sucesso o governo da Califórnia no início deste ano, é um dos poucos bilionários que declararam que votarão a favor do imposto. Steyer afirmou que, embora considere "problemática" a forma como a medida foi redigida, ela é necessária para proteger os californianos mais vulneráveis.

Huang também declarou que apoia o pagamento do imposto.

"Não me importo de pagar impostos. Quanto mais você ganha, mais impostos paga. Para mim, tudo bem", afirmou o presidente da Nvidia em uma entrevista à CBS, parceira americana da BBC. "Eu sou a personificação do sonho americano."

O senador Bernie Sanders, do estado de Vermont, conhecido por sua atuação contra a desigualdade de renda, tem feito campanha em apoio à Proposição 40.

Durante um ato em Los Angeles, Sanders disse que os bilionários "acreditam, assim como os monarcas do século 19, que têm um direito divino de governar".

"Eles têm toda a riqueza, têm todo o poder, e quem diabos vocês pensam que são para desafiá-los? Bem, acho que em 3 de novembro eles vão aprender uma lição muito importante."

O senador americano Bernie Sanders discursa no comício "Votos Acima de Bilionários" em 5 de outubro, em Los Angeles. — Foto: Getty Images via BBC

A desigualdade de renda nos Estados Unidos está entre os níveis mais altos em mais de três décadas. No terceiro trimestre de 2025, o 1% mais rico das famílias detinha quase 32% de toda a riqueza do país. Na Califórnia, a desigualdade também está próxima de níveis historicamente elevados.

A desigualdade econômica preocupa a maioria dos californianos. Segundo uma pesquisa estadual do Instituto de Políticas Públicas da Califórnia, 72% acreditam que a distância entre ricos e pobres está aumentando, e uma proporção semelhante considera que o governo estadual deveria fazer mais para reduzir essa diferença.

Trebbi afirma que a política é impulsionada por um "sentimento antielite e antissistema".

"Na verdade, isso não se trata da Proposição 40", diz ele, mas de uma tentativa de "reequilibrar um pouco a balança".

articles.title: É hora de comprar ações? Veja o que avaliar após o tombo do Ibovespa | G1
articles.standfirst: Queda da bolsa pode abrir oportunidades em empresas negociadas com desconto, mas juros altos, incertezas fiscais e dificuldades financeiras de companhias elevam o risco de novas perdas.
articles.summary: Queda da bolsa pode abrir oportunidades em empresas negociadas com desconto, mas juros altos, incertezas fiscais e dificuldades financeiras de companhias elevam o risco.
articles.body:
A forte queda da bolsa brasileira após a reeleição de Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT), nesta segunda-feira (26), levantou uma dúvida entre investidores: é hora de aproveitar os preços mais baixos para comprar ações ou esperar que o mercado se estabilize?

O Ibovespa recuou 13,88% , aos 176.608 pontos , registrando a maior queda diária desde março de 2020, no início da pandemia de Covid-19. No dia 20 daquele mês, o índice caiu 13,92% .

Com a queda desta segunda-feira, a bolsa brasileira perdeu R$ 734 bilhões em valor de mercado, segundo levantamento da Elos Ayta. O montante equivale a quase todo o valor de mercado da Petrobras, estimado em R$ 746 bilhões .

👉 A reação refletiu a surpresa de parte dos investidores com o resultado eleitoral. Quem esperava uma transição para um governo de centro-direita passou a rever suas estratégias diante das incertezas sobre a condução da economia, os gastos públicos e o controle da dívida do governo.

A queda dos preços, porém, não significa que todas as ações estejam baratas nem que seja o momento ideal para comprá-las. Segundo especialistas consultados pelo g1 , a decisão depende das condições de cada empresa, de sua capacidade de gerar resultados e do tamanho de suas dívidas.

Queda não significa que todas as ações estão baratas

Olívia Flôres de Brás, CEO da Magno Investimentos, ressalta que a queda no preço das ações não significa, necessariamente, que uma empresa perdeu capacidade de gerar resultados.

Para avaliar se um papel está barato, é preciso comparar seu preço de mercado com os resultados que a companhia pode alcançar.

"Uma queda de 10% tampouco significa que as empresas perderam, de um dia para o outro, 10% de sua capacidade de gerar resultados. Significa que os investidores passaram a aceitar preços menores diante dos riscos percebidos.”

Segundo ela, em um cenário econômico mais incerto, os investidores passam a exigir uma compensação maior pelo risco de aplicar seu dinheiro.

👉 Por isso, uma ação que ficou mais barata pode representar uma oportunidade de compra se a empresa mantiver boas perspectivas de resultados . Se a expectativa de lucro piorar ou o custo para financiar as atividades aumentar, porém, a queda do preço pode não ser suficiente para tornar o papel atrativo.

Essa ressalva também aparece na análise da Vault Research, que atribui parte da queda à reversão das apostas de investidores em uma transição para um governo de centro-direita.

As 10 maiores quedas do Ibovespa em 26 de outubro — Foto: Arte/g1

Segundo a corretora, cerca de US$ 4 bilhões ( R$ 21,5 bilhões ) haviam entrado na bolsa em outubro com essa expectativa. Com a reeleição de Lula, esses investidores passaram a desfazer suas posições, pressionando os preços das ações.

Para a Vault, no entanto, a reação ao resultado eleitoral não explica todos os riscos envolvidos.

Os analistas também apontam problemas na situação fiscal do país, na inflação e na saúde financeira das empresas, fatores que podem comprometer os resultados dos negócios.

“Mesmo depois do tombo, o Ibovespa segue cerca de 9% acima do início do ano, com fiscal, inflação e balanço das empresas piores. Pode haver alívio pontual, mas a direção é de queda.”

Exportadoras e empresas defensivas entram no radar

Diante dos riscos para a bolsa, o BTG Pactual recomenda cautela na escolha das ações.

O banco alerta para a possibilidade de novas perdas, em meio à alta dos juros de longo prazo, e prioriza empresas que recebem parte de suas receitas em moeda estrangeira, têm menos dívidas ou atuam em setores menos sensíveis às oscilações da economia.

"As perspectivas de um real mais fraco podem favorecer as ações de exportadoras, como as produtoras de commodities metálicas, petróleo e gás, commodities agrícolas e exportadoras industriais”, dizem os analistas.

Entre as exportadoras citadas pelo BTG estão Gerdau , Suzano , Vale , PRIO , SLC Agrícola , 3Tentos , S ão Martinho , WEG e Embraer . Algumas delas estiveram entre as poucas ações do Ibovespa que fecharam em alta nesta segunda-feira. ( veja mais abaixo )

🔎 Isso ocorre porque a alta do dólar pode elevar, em reais, o valor das receitas obtidas com vendas ao exterior. O efeito sobre os resultados, porém, depende dos custos, das dívidas e da exposição cambial de cada empresa.

Além das exportadoras, o BTG destaca empresas menos endividadas e com maior capacidade de enfrentar períodos de juros elevados. São as chamadas “ações defensivas” , que, segundo os analistas, tendem a apresentar desempenho relativamente melhor nesse cenário.

“Empresas com balanços fortes (baixa alavancagem ou posição de caixa líquido) e que atuam em setores defensivos também devem se sair relativamente bem. Seguradoras como Caixa Seguridade e Porto Seguro e a fabricante de bebidas Ambev devem apresentar desempenho superior.”

O banco também destaca a Petrobras e o Itaú Unibanco entre as grandes empresas da bolsa.

No caso da estatal, a exposição ao petróleo, a proteção cambial e a distribuição de dividendos são apontadas como fatores favoráveis. Já o Itaú é considerado pelo BTG o grande banco mais bem preparado para enfrentar cenários econômicos adversos.

Apenas 8 ações fecharam em alta nesta segunda-feira (26) — Foto: Arte/g1

Juros altos e incerteza fiscal aumentam os riscos para a bolsa

Para avaliar se a queda das ações representa uma oportunidade de compra, também é preciso considerar a capacidade das empresas de enfrentar um período prolongado de juros elevados.

Além de encarecer novos empréstimos, esse cenário dificulta o pagamento de dívidas já existentes e pode limitar os recursos disponíveis para investimentos e expansão dos negócios.

🔎 Os dados sobre a situação financeira das empresas ajudam a dimensionar esse risco: em 2025, o Brasil registrou 977 processos de recuperação judicial, que envolveram 2.466 empresas. O número de CNPJs foi o maior da série histórica da Serasa Experian, iniciada em 2012. Em agosto de 2026, dado mais recente disponível, o país tinha 9,3 milhões de empresas inadimplentes, com R$ 244,4 bilhões em dívidas negativadas.

Os riscos para a bolsa, porém, não se limitam à situação financeira das companhias. O desempenho do mercado também dependerá das expectativas sobre as contas públicas e das decisões do governo para a economia.

Para o Goldman Sachs, a situação fiscal continuará sendo o principal fator considerado pelos investidores na avaliação do risco brasileiro.

Segundo Alberto Ramos, chefe da equipe de Pesquisa Econômica para a América Latina da divisão de Pesquisa de Investimentos Globais do banco, a reação dos mercados após o resultado eleitoral dependerá dos sinais do governo sobre a política econômica.

Entre os pontos de atenção estão a escolha do ministro da Fazenda e a apresentação de um plano mais claro para equilibrar as contas públicas nos próximos quatro anos.

A composição do Congresso também pode dificultar a aprovação de medidas econômicas. O Partido Liberal (PL) tem a maior bancada da Câmara , com 121 deputados, e 29 senadores no Senado. Para Ramos, essa configuração pode ampliar os obstáculos à articulação política do governo Lula.

“Dada a composição mais à direita do Congresso, o presidente Lula provavelmente enfrentará desafios ainda maiores do que no mandato atual por conta do bloco de oposição conservadora maior e pelo fato de seu capital político ser limitado, visto que não poderá buscar a reeleição em 2030”, argumenta Ramos.

Painel da B3 - Bovespa — Foto: Nelson Almeida/ AFP

articles.title: JPMorgan's CEO just sent a memo to anyone watching the U.S. economy
articles.summary: JPMorgan just posted a strong quarter. What Dimon said alongside the numbers is worth a closer look.
articles.body:
JPMorgan Chase recently delivered another big quarter. The bank earned $15.3 billion, or $5.57 a share, in the third quarter, though the results fell short of Wall Street's estimates in a rare miss, CNBC reported .

Revenue still climbed 8% from a year earlier.

Yet the more telling part of the report sat beneath the profit. Jamie Dimon used it to flag a short list of risks building under a still-strong economy.

In an interview days later, he described the U.S. economy as booming, while warning that inflationary events could still push prices higher.

The 5 economic threats JPMorgan is watching

Dimon named them in one sentence: large fiscal deficits, sticky inflation, elevated asset prices, rising interest rates, and geopolitical conditions "continue to shift under the surface," he said, according to JPMorgan's earnings release .

These forces may be manageable, he added, but the bank remains prepared for a wide range of outcomes.

Washington's borrowing tops the list. The federal government closed fiscal 2026 with a deficit of about $1.99 trillion, which was $217 billion wider than the year before. The debt pile hasn't stopped growing either, reaching roughly $40.39 trillion on Oct. 15.

Inflation and interest rates are tangled together. In May, a spike in crude oil sent the Consumer Price Index to 4.2%, its highest reading in three years, CBS News reported .

The Fed answered in September by raising rates for the first time since 2023 and hinted that another hike could come this year. Fed Chair Kevin Warsh said plainly that inflation had stayed too high for too long.

The last two threats are harder to measure. Dimon has pointed to the remilitarization of the world and the restructuring of trade as forces that could raise prices, and inflation has risen during the Iran conflict.

On the earnings call, he also acknowledged that times are good, with high asset prices and fairly low credit losses. Elevated valuations leave less room for error if any of the other four threats flare up.

How America's biggest banks are protecting themselves

On the balance sheet, JPMorgan is padding its cushion. It set aside $2.7 billion for credit losses during the quarter, and $539 million of that went into reserves, mostly for wholesale loans.

The bank also pulled back on share buybacks. Actual losses are still in check, though, since net charge-offs came in lower than a year ago.

Dimon is also getting pickier about who gets a loan. "We are tightening up a little bit credit," he told analysts , adding that some credit terms have become a little looser. In plain terms, the bank is being more careful about the loans it makes.

articles.title: Meta seeks up to $95bn in equity
articles.summary: Meta Platforms Inc is seeking to raise as much as $95 billion from selling common and preferred stock, supporting its development in AI with one of the
articles.body: Meta Platforms Inc is seeking to raise as much as $95 billion from selling common and preferred stock, supporting its development in AI with one of the largest equity offerings in history. The company is offering about $35 billion of common and preferred stock, according to a statement Monday. It also plans to raise as much as $60 billion in an at-the-market share sale programme, which allows companies to sell shares in the open market from time to time. articles.body: Nifty gainers and losers: Tata Consumer jumps 6.2%, Hindustan Unilever drops 3.2% Tata Consumer Products led Nifty 50 gainers in early trade, rising 6.20%, followed by Bharat Electronics (2.23%), Bajaj Auto (1.39%), Sun Pharma (1.33%) and Maruti Suzuki (1.29%). Hindustan Unilever was the biggest loser, falling 3.21%, followed by Infosys (2.81%), TCS (2.05%), HCL Technologies (1.31%) and Asian Paints (1.25%). The Nifty 50 was down 23.25 points, or 0.10%, at 22,729.95 around 9:54 am. .Sensex trade flat; BEL, Maruti top gainers, Hindustan Unilever sinks 3% Indian equity benchmarks traded marginally lower in early trade, with the Sensex down 90.53 points, or 0.12%, at 73,516.22 around 9:54 am. The Nifty also remained under pressure. On the Sensex, Bharat Electronics led gainers, rising 2.17%, followed by Maruti Suzuki (1.46%), Power Grid (1.24%), Sun Pharma (1.23%) and Bharti Airtel (1.16%). Hindustan Unilever was the biggest laggard, falling 3.12%, followed by Infosys (2.73%), TCS (2.05%), HCL Technologies (1.41%) and Asian Paints (1.35%)..Nifty falls up about 50 points in early trade The NSE Nifty 50 fell traded about 50 points lower in early trade, while touching an intraday low of 22,653.20, before recovering some losses. The index had opened at 73,484.38, compared with the previous close of 73,606.75, and touched an intraday low of 73,210.76 till 9.30am. .Nifty opens 44 points lower at 22,708 The NSE Nifty 50 opened 44.40 points, or 0.20%, lower at 22,708.80, against the previous close of 22,753.20..Stock Market Today: Sensex opens 122 points lower at 73,484 The BSE Sensex opened 122.37 points, or 0.17%, lower at 73,484.38 on Tuesday, against the previous close of 73,606.75..Rupee rises 2 paise to 95.13 against US dollar in early trade .Australian shares fall 0.3% as bank stocks slide; inflation data in focus Australian shares fell as losses in financial and healthcare stocks outweighed gains in mining and energy shares. The S&P/ASX 200 slipped 0.3% to 8,783, with all four major banks declining as investors awaited quarterly inflation data due Wednesday for clues on the Reserve Bank of Australia’s next rate decision. Mining stocks gained 1.1% on firmer copper prices, while Star Entertainment surged as much as 21.7% after reporting a quarterly profit. New Zealand’s S&P/NZX 50 fell 0.8% ahead of its central bank’s policy decision. .Japan’s Nikkei jumps 1.9% as Anthropic IPO filing boosts AI stocks Japan’s Nikkei rose 1.91%, heading for a recovery after three consecutive sessions of losses, as Anthropic’s IPO filing and a rally in US semiconductor stocks lifted AI-linked shares. Chip-testing equipment maker Advantest surged 10%, while SoftBank Group gained 6.94% and Tokyo Electron rose 3.35%. However, gains were uneven, with investors cautious ahead of earnings from US technology giants Alphabet and Microsoft. .South Korea’s Kospi surges 4.4% on AI stock rally, stronger-than-expected GDP growth South Korean shares jumped, led by chipmakers Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix, which gained 5.05% and 7.14%, respectively, as a rally in US AI stocks lifted sentiment. The benchmark Kospi rose 4.39% to 5,709.85 after data showed the economy grew faster than expected in the third quarter, supported by the global AI chip boom. Foreign investors were net buyers of shares worth 597.3 billion won, while the Korean won strengthened against the dollar. .Sensex, Nifty likely to open lower as oil stays near six-month high; Fed decision in focus Indian benchmark indices are set for a weak start, with GIFT Nifty indicating losses as Brent crude hovers near $115 a barrel and investors await the US Federal Reserve’s policy decision. The Sensex and Nifty rose 0.7% on Monday, snapping a four-session losing streak. Foreign investors continued to sell Indian equities, offloading Rs 1,462 crore on Monday. Tata Consumer Products, Paytm and Nazara Technologies are among the stocks to watch after their quarterly earnings. .Asian markets mixed as tech stocks rally on Wall Street after Anthropic IPO filing Asian markets traded mixed, with South Korea’s Kospi jumping 4% and Japan’s Nikkei rising 1.9% as technology stocks tracked Wall Street gains following AI firm Anthropic’s IPO filing. Hong Kong and Shanghai edged lower as investors awaited key corporate earnings from Microsoft, Alphabet, Amazon, Samsung and SK hynix, along with the US Federal Reserve’s interest rate decision on Wednesday. Oil prices extended their decline amid diplomatic efforts to ease Middle East tensions.

articles.title: Instagram tests 90-minute horizontal videos - what it means for long-form content creators
articles.summary: Instagram on Monday began testing new features, including 90-minute horizontal videos to target long-form content creators like podcasters and comedians,
articles.body: Instagram on Monday began testing new features, including 90-minute horizontal videos to target long-form content creators like podcasters and comedians, with select creators in the US.The feature, called “Features”, will allow them to link short reel clips, typically around three minutes or less, to full-length videos, as per The Hollywood Reporter.“What you’re now going to be able to do is, you see a clip of a podcast that you love, you can just click and continue watching or watch the full video, and you’ll be able to dive in and see the whole thing because creators are going to be able to link these Reels to their overall feature,” vice-president of product at Instagram, Tessa Lyons, said.Instagram has already been testing Features with creators in Brazil and plans to expand the trial to tens of thousands of creators in the US. The videos will reportedly be recommended to users through the Explore page and other areas of the platform.The feature will be available on mobile, with Instagram aiming to extend the viewing experience to its TV app. Instagram for TV, which launched last year and is available on Samsung, Fire TV and Google TV, is now expanding to Apple TV in the US.“We think the best viewing experience for longform horizontal content is on a big, horizontal screen, and so I think that is where we will expect a lot of the deep consumption to happen over time,” Lyons said, as per The Hollywood Reporter.Instagram is also experimenting with “Series”, a feature that gives episodic Reels a dedicated space on a creator’s profile. The move comes amid growing interest in microdramas and episodic videos among creators.In June, the company began reaching out to microdrama studios in Southeast Asia to test the feature. It has since approached individual creators who have been experimenting with episodic content.Instagram plans to begin testing Series in more countries in the coming months, with a US launch targeted for the end of this year or early next year. The company has also started testing how the feature will appear on television.Other experiments include integrating live videos into the Reels tab and recommending them to users who do not follow the creators. The test is launching in Indonesia and Brazil, with an expansion to the US planned for next year.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Piyush Goyal holds talks with global tech and manufacturing firms on India investment opportunities
articles.summary: Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal has held discussions with executives of semiconductor equipment maker ASML, chipmaker Nexperia, IKEA operator
articles.body: Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal has held discussions with executives of semiconductor equipment maker ASML, chipmaker Nexperia, IKEA operator Ingka Group and clean-energy company Power2X, as India seeks to attract investment and expand cooperation with European businesses in technology, manufacturing and renewable energy.The meetings took place during Goyal’s visit to the Netherlands, which included the India-Netherlands Business Forum in The Hague on Monday. The minister used the forum to pitch India as an investment destination, highlighting its growing consumer market, manufacturing capabilities and opportunities in emerging industries.In a post on X, Goyal said his meeting with Wayne Allan, executive vice-president and member of ASML’s board of management, focused on advanced semiconductor technologies, innovation and skill development. “With a strong policy push in India, growing investments, and an expanding talent pool, we explored avenues for collaboration in cutting-edge semiconductor technologies, innovation, and skilling to strengthen India's position in the global chip value chain,” Goyal said.Discussions with Stefan Tilgner, interim CEO of Nexperia, centred on expanding semiconductor cooperation. Goyal said India’s growing electronics manufacturing capabilities and technology ecosystem offered opportunities to strengthen partnerships and build more resilient supply chains.Goyal also met Juvencio Maeztu, CEO and president of Ingka Group, which operates IKEA, to discuss manufacturing and sourcing opportunities. “Discussed opportunities offered by our growing consumer market & how IKEA can leverage India's manufacturing capabilities to strengthen its global sourcing network,” he said.The minister’s meeting with Occo Roelofsen, founder and CEO of Power2X, focused on India-Netherlands cooperation in green hydrogen, renewable energy and emerging technologies.Addiitonally, at the India-Netherlands Business Forum, Goyal called on European businesses to deepen their engagement with India and argued that companies needed fewer regulatory hurdles and simpler procedures. “The world wants deregulation. The world wants more freedom. The business world is looking for less compliance burden, simpler processes, simpler procedures, less paperwork,” he said.Goyal also highlighted the investment potential of India’s expanding power capacity and growing clean-energy base, particularly for data centres and other energy-intensive industries. He said the sector could attract around $200 billion in investments over the coming years.His remarks came amid a broader debate over the European Union’s regulatory framework and its Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM). Dutch mMinister for foreign trade and development cooperation Sjoerd Sjoerdsma defended regulations covering climate, product quality and safety, while saying rules that unnecessarily hinder trade should be reviewed.You use AI every day. articles.title: AI makes discoveries in mathematics, computer science, physics, OpenAI says
articles.summary: OpenAI’s announcement is the latest in a series of claimed scientific breakthroughs credited to AI.
articles.body:
OpenAI has announced that its AI models have made several scientific discoveries in mathematics, computer science and physics.

The AI giant said on Monday that the three new discoveries concerned the fields of harmonic analysis, complexity theory and quantum field theory.

Among the discoveries, AI models proved the local smoothing conjecture, one of the central propositions of harmonic analysis, in every spatial dimension for the first time, according to OpenAI.

Researchers in harmonic analysis, a branch of mathematics that studies how complex signals and functions can be broken down into elementary waves, had previously only proved the theory in three dimensions.

Alex Iosevich, a professor of mathematics at the University of Rochester who specialises in harmonic analysis, said OpenAI appeared to have “cracked” the conjecture in a “historic development”.

“The conjecture was formulated by my PhD adviser, Chris Sogge, so it is near and dear to my heart, and the news was a shock at first,” Iosevich told Al Jazeera.

“Now I am filled with joy and optimism, because the scientific enterprise as a whole is going to make giant leaps as a result of the AI revolution, and we have the chance to be a part of this historic development.”

Iosevich said he expected the field of theoretical mathematics to “change drastically” due to AI.

“I feel a twinge of sadness as a result,” Iosevich said.

“Many theoretical mathematicians I know feel the same way, but I firmly believe that these feelings will soon give way to the realisation that there is so much we can now accomplish.”

“Problems in pure mathematics did not arise in a vacuum,” he added. “Many of them came out of concrete physical considerations, and these connections can now be explored rapidly and decisively.”

According to OpenAI’s announcement, its models also disproved the Exponential Time Hypothesis, which relates to the time it takes to solve complex computational problems, and provided “mathematically rigorous [proof of the] existence” of quantum chromodynamics, which studies the interaction of quarks and gluons.

The ChatGPT creator said it had reached out to scientists outside the company to turn its “raw research data into scientific understanding”.

The San Francisco-based company said it decided on several different methods for releasing the findings based on consultations with three expert groups chosen to act as “shepherds”.

While the groups collaborating on the mathematics and computer science problems opted to make the AI-produced data public immediately, the physics group decided to defer the release in order to write up their own interpretation of the findings, OpenAI said.

“All of these approaches involve tradeoffs,” OpenAI said.

“On the one hand, the collaborations empower experts to foster unpacking the results and contextualizing them in the broader academic community,” the $852bn start-up said.

“On the other hand, choosing initial shepherds necessarily shapes who gets involved first and creates asymmetry of information. We welcome feedback on how to broaden participation and make this process more useful.”

OpenAI’s announcement is the latest in a series of claimed scientific breakthroughs credited to AI.

Last month, Claude creator Anthropic announced the discovery of a new enzyme said to resemble CRISPR , the groundbreaking gene editing mechanism used in treating conditions such as cancer and sickle cell disease.

Anthropic’s announcement drew mixed reactions among scientists.

While some researchers hailed the finding as an exciting development, others suggested that the AI company had exaggerated its significance.

articles.title: How AI-powered tools are helping Indian investors turn market data into smart decisions
articles.summary: The rapid expansion of global capital markets has created an unprecedented era of retail access.
articles.body: The rapid expansion of global capital markets has created an unprecedented era of retail access. Today, millions of people worldwide can instantly track a dizzying array of financial instruments from their mobile devices. From traditional equities and physical commodities to digital assets, the sheer volume of information available at our fingertips is staggering.For decades, the primary hurdle for the everyday investor was simply getting a seat at the table. Now that the gates are open, this newfound accessibility has introduced a completely different and equally daunting fundamental problem for the modern market participant.The new challenge: From data access to data interpretationAccess to raw data is no longer the primary barrier to entry; the overarching challenge now lies in properly interpreting that data. Having real-time price feeds, intricate candlestick charts, and continuous macroeconomic updates means very little if a user lacks the time or technical expertise to make sense of them.The global financial landscape has become heavily oversaturated with information. Retail traders often find themselves competing against institutional algorithms, leaving many participants feeling overwhelmed by the very platforms meant to empower them. Without the right analytical tools, tracking multiple asset classes across different time zones can easily lead to decision fatigue, preventing everyday people from executing strategies with clarity or confidence.To bridge this significant knowledge gap, artificial intelligence is stepping in as the ultimate market equaliser. Rather than simply throwing more numerical data at users, the next generation of financial technology leverages advanced machine learning models to help people interpret complex market signals and take decisive, independent action. This marks a vital shift from passive information gathering to active, actionable intelligence. By translating dense technical indicators into plain language, these intelligent systems fundamentally change how everyday participants interact with capital markets, ensuring that advanced analytical capabilities are no longer strictly reserved for quantitative firms and professional analysts.Recognising this critical need for clarity, Binance has unveiled Binance Intelligence, a comprehensive artificial intelligence suite built directly into its core user experience¹. The central philosophy driving this launch starts at the root problem for many users, which is providing the exact tools required to interpret overwhelming financial information and act on it seamlessly¹. This new capability layer is not a sudden pivot, but rather the culmination of extensive backend development. Over the past several years, the company has built and successfully deployed over one hundred distinct artificial intelligence models across its rigorous compliance and risk management systems²."Finance shouldn't ask you to become an expert first," explained Richard Teng, CEO of Binance. "It should meet you where you are. With Binance Intelligence, it does."Now, Binance Intelligence takes everything learned from securing those complex networks and puts it directly into the products that users rely on daily¹.Reimagining financial access through tiered solutionsTo reshape how finance works for its global audience, the platform has introduced a meticulously designed suite of three distinct products tailored for varying levels of technical proficiency².The foundational tool for the everyday user is Binance AI, which operates as a completely free, round-the-clock personal assistant². This intuitive feature allows individuals to ask natural questions, receive immediate help interpreting market dynamics, and navigate complex trading environments without needing to decipher dense documentation. For the Indian user juggling multiple portfolios, often across different asset classes, this 24/7 assistant can answer questions like "How will US Fed policy impact Bitcoin?" or "What technical indicators should I watch?" in simple, conversational language.For users seeking to automate their specific trading strategies without writing complex scripts, Binance AI Pro offers the unprecedented ability to build sophisticated trading workflows entirely through a simple, no-code interface². This effectively democratizes algorithmic trading, allowing casual users to construct automated actions based on specific market triggers. Consider an investor who wants to automatically execute trades when certain technical indicators align during off-hours. Previously, this would require coding skills or hiring a developer. With AI Pro's no-code interface, they can build these strategies themselves, democratising tools once available only to professional algorithmic trading firms.Furthermore, the rollout caters heavily to the professional developer community with the introduction of BinanceAgent OS². This advanced foundational infrastructure allows builders to create highly capable artificial intelligence agents integrated directly with native platform capabilities². Developers can now build sophisticated market actors that operate with low latency and deep market access.By providing these tiered, interoperable solutions, the ecosystem ensures that everyone from casual traders trying to understand yield mechanics to quantitative developers building high-frequency bots has the exact right tools to participate securely and efficiently².Building confidence through intelligent infrastructureFor investors everywhere, security and regulatory compliance are paramount concerns, especially in emerging asset classes. Binance Intelligence's foundation in the platform's existing compliance infrastructure means these AI tools operate within the same rigorous security framework that processes millions of transactions daily. Having AI-powered tools that can help users understand both market dynamics and their own risk exposure becomes increasingly valuable as global regulatory landscapes continue to evolve.Meeting users where they areThe ultimate objective of this new intelligence layer is to permanently eliminate the intimidation factor historically associated with global capital markets. As part of a broader vision for 2026, the company is focused on making the technological complexities of digital assets practically invisible to the end user.For diverse investor bases globally, from small-town traders to metropolitan professionals, from students making their first investments to seasoned investors managing substantial portfolios, this democratisation of market intelligence represents a significant step forward.By transforming an ocean of raw data into clear, accessible pathways, this new suite of tools proves that the future of finance is not just about providing more information. It is about empowering users to understand that information and act on it with confidence.*You must be at least 18 years old to access this siteemail id : pr@binance.comReferences:Binance Intelligence - Blog. articles.title: NHAI sets 3-month deadline to improve ‘look and feel’ of national highways
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) has identified over two dozen items for improvement over the next three months to enhance “look and
articles.body: NEW DELHI: National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) has identified over two dozen items for improvement over the next three months to enhance “look and feel” of national highways and improve commuters' experience. The exercise will focus on rectifying road defects, improving safety features, maintaining cleanliness and upgrading highway infrastructure.TOI has learnt that the authority has asked all its regional officers, project directors and highway contractors to focus on these areas. The identified measures include filling potholes, repairing cracked road surfaces, addressing visible rutting, restoring faded pavement markings and fixing damaged kerbs. NHAI has also flagged defunct highway lighting, damaged road signs and overhead sign structures, broken concrete barriers and faded paintwork for rectification.The authority will use dashcam footage to identify defects that need to be fixed. Other priorities include dressing uneven earthen shoulders, removing vegetation, ensuring proper median plantation, replacing missing drain covers and closing unauthorised openings in road medians. Unauthorised signboards, hoardings and encroachments will also be addressed.Work-zone safety and proper arrangements for traffic diversions are among the items identified for immediate attention.In addition, NHAI has proposed providing an adequate number of road studs, installing impact attenuators (crash cushions) at hazardous locations and adding gantries where required. The plan also covers improving the quality of toilets, painting foot overbridges and gantries, refurbishing bus bays and deploying road-sweeping and drain-cleaning machines.The authority has also identified toll plaza approaches, service roads, waterlogging, highway slopes and approaches to structures for improvement. Measures include better signage, road markings and landscaping near toll plazas, smoother riding surfaces and preventing water ponding.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: The accountability gap: Why traditional identity checks fail in an automated world
articles.summary: A wire transfer clears at midnight. A complex compliance alert is investigated and closed seconds later.
articles.body: A wire transfer clears at midnight. A complex compliance alert is investigated and closed seconds later. A sanctions list is cross-referenced against a global database without a single human investigator clicking a mouse. This is the new reality of autonomous finance. Software has stopped merely suggesting actions; it is now executing them.Artificial intelligence is no longer just a digital assistant waiting for a prompt. It is becoming an independent actor capable of moving capital, investigating cases, tracing funds across chains, and altering records. This shift from software that assists to software that acts is testing the limits of global regulatory frameworks. Handing the operational reins to autonomous systems offers a massive structural advantage. These digital actors can process vast amounts of fragmented data and prioritise severe threats in milliseconds, freeing human experts to tackle complex, judgment-based casework.However, this newfound autonomy creates a glaring blind spot. The entire global financial system is built on a single, foundational question: who is the customer. Today, knowing the entity behind an account is simply not enough to prevent financial crime. A verification check might prove that a specific corporation owns an account, but it fails to identify the compromised sub-program that initiated an unauthorised payment.Knowing the customer does not explain whether an instruction came from that person, an authorised digital assistant, or a rogue secondary program operating well outside its intended mandate. Consider a scenario where two software programs access the same financial platform. One only has permission to read historical data, while the other possesses the authority to alter a risk profile and execute a trade. Traditional identity verification cannot explain which digital actor pulled the trigger, under whose mandate it operated, or who should be held responsible.Global regulatory bodies are moving aggressively to close this widening accountability gap. The Monetary Authority of Singapore recently introduced its SAFR framework, focusing on runtime safeguards and auditability for automated financial applications. Similarly, the Financial Services AI Adoption Plan in the United Kingdom explicitly demands interoperable machine-to-machine authentication protocols and recommends a specific protocol for agentic payments. International observers share this urgency. The International Monetary Fund notes that the industry is experiencing a distinct transition from a manual "click-to-pay" world to an automated "decide-to-pay" reality. These policy signals indicate a growing consensus among regulators that as software gains the power to initiate payments and move value autonomously, institutional governance must strictly follow that authority.To address this structural vulnerability head-on, the Binance Global Policy team has outlined a comprehensive architecture for autonomous compliance. In a recent insights paper authored by Steven McWhirter and Diego Montes Serralde, with expert contribution from Tanveer Kalooji, the team proposes a novel framework called "Know Your Agent" to manage this transition safely¹.This protocol is specifically designed to sit alongside existing regulatory obligations rather than replace them¹. It acts as a highly complementary layer to traditional customer verification, anti-money laundering controls, the Travel Rule, and established sanctions obligations¹. By implementing this framework, institutions can establish exactly who a digital actor is, who it represents, what actions it is permitted to execute, and who ultimately remains responsible for its behaviour¹.A five-layer architecture for accountabilityThe proposed protocol is built on five functional layers designed to track a digital actor from deployment to execution¹. The first requires clear agent identity and provenance, ensuring each piece of software carries a distinct identity linked to its provider, deployer, and specific version¹. The second establishes a definitive link to an accountable principal, meaning the software is permanently tied to the person or legal entity responsible for its deployment¹.The third enforces strict mandates and permissions based on least-privilege access, separating the ability to recommend an action from the authority to actually execute it¹. The fourth introduces authenticated delegation chains combined with continuous behavioural and transactional monitoring¹. If an actor delegates a task to a sub-program, that chain of command must be authenticated and tracked in real time¹. Finally, the fifth layer guarantees absolute revocation and auditability¹. Institutions must possess an immediate mechanism to suspend a rogue program, ensuring every material action can be traced backward to its original principal¹.The principle of bounded autonomyThis layered architecture creates a secure system defined by bounded autonomy¹. Within this structured ecosystem, automated systems are free to analyse massive datasets, prioritise operational alerts, and recommend compliance solutions without creating human bottlenecks¹. Consequential actions, however, remain trapped behind deterministic, rules-based controls that the software simply cannot bypass¹. The framework dictates that any action with material financial consequence demands proportionate human or institutional oversight¹. The underlying logic is straightforward: increased operational autonomy and a greater potential for market disruption must always trigger stronger identity verification and more rigorous approval thresholds¹.The ultimate goal of this framework is to ensure that technological advancement does not erode regulatory transparency or institutional responsibility. "We’ve built much of financial crime compliance around knowing the customer. But in an agentic world, that is no longer enough," explained Steven McWhirter, Global Head of Policy at Binance¹. "When software can investigate, decide and move money, we need to be able to say with confidence which agent acted, on whose authority, and who remains accountable. Know Your Agent isn’t about giving software legal personality; it’s about preserving accountability as autonomy scales. Autonomy should never outrun our ability to verify, bound and, where necessary, revoke it¹."Three lenses of future complianceAs the digital economy matures, the foundational architecture of financial crime prevention must evolve to accommodate this new technology. The most secure markets of the future will rely on three intersecting pillars to maintain integrity. They will need traditional verification frameworks to know the customer, continuous monitoring tools to know the transaction, and modern protocols to know the agent.By building these strict governance layers directly into the core infrastructure, the global financial sector can unlock the massive efficiency gains of automation without surrendering regulatory accountability.*You must be at least 18 years old to access this siteemail id : pr@binance.comReferences: Binance Blog. articles.title: India-US trade portal sees 3,500 registrations within months of launch, says Piyush Goyal
articles.summary: The India-US Trade Facilitation Portal has attracted around 3,500 registrations within months of its launch, commerce and industry minister Piyush Goyal
articles.body: The India-US Trade Facilitation Portal has attracted around 3,500 registrations within months of its launch, commerce and industry minister Piyush Goyal said, highlighting its role in helping Indian exporters, particularly MSMEs and first-time exporters, connect with American buyers.In a post on X, Goyal described the response as encouraging and said the initiative was creating new opportunities for businesses in both countries to establish partnerships and expand their presence in international markets. “Trust. Trade. Opportunities. This Trade Facilitation Portal is a landmark initiative seamlessly connecting businesses on both sides,” Goyal said.The portal is a digital business-to-business (B2B) marketplace launched by the Consulate General of India in New York, in collaboration with other Indian consulates in the United States and the Indian Embassy in Washington DC.Designed to facilitate trade between Indian exporters and US buyers, the platform provides a common digital space where businesses can showcase products, identify potential partners and explore commercial opportunities across sectors.It offers category-wise product listings, search tools and personalised dashboards to help users track business leads, monitor trade activity and assess engagement. The platform also hosts virtual exhibitions and curated product showcases, allowing exporters to reach potential buyers without relying solely on physical trade events.The initiative is aimed at simplifying cross-border business interactions and making the US market more accessible to smaller Indian enterprises seeking international customers.Highlighting its potential, Goyal said, “It will open up new opportunities for Indian businesses, particularly MSMEs & first-time exporters, to forge partnerships, explore new markets & expand their global reach.”The registrations mark an early response to the initiative as India seeks to strengthen business-to-business engagement with the United States and widen export opportunities for smaller enterprises.You use AI every day. articles.title: South Korea’s GDP growth beats forecasts amid AI boom
articles.summary: Asia’s fourth-largest economy grows 3.4 percent year-on-year amid strong semiconductor demand.
articles.body:
South Korea’s economy grew much faster than expected in the July-September quarter amid booming demand for chips used in artificial intelligence (AI).

Gross domestic product (GDP) expanded 1 percent on a quarterly basis, or 3.4 percent year-on-year, advance estimates released by the Bank of Korea showed on Tuesday.

The Bank of Korea forecast in August that GDP would grow 0.3 percent in the third quarter.

Exports, which account for about 45 percent of South Korea’s GDP, rose 2.3 percent quarter-on-quarter, driven by semiconductors, machinery and electrical equipment, according to the central bank.

Investment in facilities and intellectual property rose 4.1 percent and 2.3 percent, respectively, while investment in construction edged up 0.7 percent.

Despite the robust growth in exports and investment, private consumption fell 0.2 percent.

The latest results put the South Korean economy well on track to achieve its biggest economic expansion in more than a decade.

South Korean Finance Minister Lee Hyoung-il said earlier this month that he expected growth to reach 3.4-3.6 percent in 2026, which would be the strongest performance since 2011, excluding the COVID-19 pandemic.

South Korea’s economy grew 1 percent in 2025, its slowest expansion since the pandemic.

Asia’s fourth-largest economy has capitalised on the AI boom amid a global shortage of memory chips.

South Korea is home to two of the three largest memory chip makers, SK Hynix and Samsung Electronics, which together control roughly 80 percent of the global market for high-bandwidth memory and 60 percent of the market for dynamic random-access memory.

South Korea’s exports in September surged 83.5 percent year-on-year to $120.9bn, with chips accounting for nearly half of all shipments, according to the Korea Customs Service.

articles.title: Precio de la luz por horas hoy, martes 27 de octubre: cuándo es más barata y más cara en el día
articles.standfirst: El precio de la luz se encarece moderadamente este martes
articles.summary: El precio de la luz se encarece moderadamente este martes
articles.body: El precio medio de la electricidad del día actual se sitúa en 206,89 €/MWh, lo que representa un incremento de 10,03 € respecto al precio medio del día anterior, que fue de 196,86 €/MWh. Este aumento se aprecia en un martes, un día típico de demanda alta. A medida que se analizan las horas más caras y más baratas, se vislumbran variaciones en los costes a lo largo de la jornada. Los precios de la electricidad alcanzan su punto máximo entre las franjas horarias de 17:00 a 20:00, donde se registran picos significativos que agravan el costo para los consumidores. Durante estas horas, se observan tarifas superiores a los 257 €/MWh, con un máximo de 283.05 €/MWh a las 18:00. Este bloque continuo de horas caras, que va desde las 17:00 hasta las 20:00, es indicativo de una demanda elevada, lo que provoca que los valores sean especialmente costosos, a diferencia de las horas de la madrugada, donde los precios son notablemente más bajos. La electricidad es más barata durante las horas nocturnas y en ciertos momentos del día, ofreciendo oportunidades significativas de ahorro. Las franjas horarias más destacadas son entre las 10:00 y 13:00, donde los precios caen a niveles que oscilan entre 107.64 €/MWh y 141.37 €/MWh y se observa un excelente umbral de ahorro especialmente entre las 12:00 y 14:00, con un mínimo de 106.12 €/MWh. Asimismo, la ventana de precios bajos se extiende en la noche, desde la 01:00 hasta las 04:00, con valores que rondan entre 209.77 €/MWh y 216.91 €/MWh, lo que permite aprovechar tramos consecutivos de precios accesibles. En la jornada del martes 27 de octubre de 2026, se ha observado una notoria concentración de horas con precios elevados, especialmente durante la tarde y la noche, lo que podría impactar considerablemente en la factura de los consumidores. Esta tendencia destaca la importancia de planificar el consumo eléctrico para aprovechar los momentos más económicos del día.

articles.title: Ather reports first profit, approves Rs 122 cr expansion
articles.summary: Ather Energy posts first quarterly profit of Rs 1.2 crore; approves Rs 122 crore expansion to boost Hosur and new Maharashtra plant capacity amid strong demand.
articles.body: Bengaluru: Ather Energy reported its first profit as higher sales, price increases and a shift towards more profitable scooter variants helped it absorb rising raw material costs. The Bengaluru-based company also approved a Rs 122 crore investment to expand production as demand outstrips supply.The electric scooter maker posted a profit of Rs 1.2 crore for the September quarter, compared with a loss of Rs 154 crore a year earlier and Rs 51 crore in the preceding quarter. Total income rose 62% year-on-year to Rs 1,527 crore, while vehicle sales increased 42% to 93,211 units.“We’re not out of the woods,” co-founder and CEO Tarun Mehta told analysts. He said the focus remained on increasing sales and production, cautioning that quarterly profits could fluctuate.Earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation (Ebitda) stood at Rs 74.2 crore, compared with a loss of Rs 90.8 crore a year earlier. The company’s earnings included Rs 62.7 crore in other income.Price increases and changes in the mix of variants sold helped offset higher costs of aluminium, copper, battery materials and plastics. However, Mehta said some margin gains from prioritising certain variants and reducing incentives were more temporary.“On the current portfolio, I would not want to push pricing up, at least over the next few quarters,” he said.The company said pre-orders more than doubled to about 1.8 lakh during the quarter. Mehta estimated that its existing stores could sell roughly 20,000 additional scooters a month if supplies were available. Its Hosur factory operated at 98% capacity utilisation during peak production.The expansion will increase Hosur’s annual vehicle capacity from 4.2 lakh to 4.95 lakh units by December. Ather’s new factory at Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar in Maharashtra is scheduled to begin commercial production in phases from December, initially with an annual capacity of five lakh units.The additional investment will raise the new factory’s planned capacity to 6.5 lakh units by the September quarter of 2027, taking combined annual capacity to about 11.4 lakh units. Mehta said installed capacity would take additional time to ramp up fully.Supply constraints have also shaped the rollout of Ather’s new Konarc scooter. The company prioritised mid-range versions over the entry-level variant to protect margins while production remained constrained.
